tasks.title: Compare CPU, CPU+GPU, and CPU+FPGA on the same QE shell
tasks.description: Run the shell-level comparison only after the clustered FPGA architecture and hardware-`cdiaghg` direction are frozen, then determine where the updated FPGA design wins or loses.

Task: Compare CPU, CPU+GPU, and CPU+FPGA on the same QE shell
Stage: experiment
User inputs: sections.experiment.hypothesis_or_validation_goal=Primary hypothesis: for QE SCF-shell workloads in which the iterative Davidson path is the dominant target and double-electron-integral acceleration is out of scope, the better v1 direction is no longer a shell model that only hardwareizes `h_psi`, `s_psi`, `build H_sub/S_sub`, and `refresh/residual -> P_next` while leaving `cdiaghg` outside. Instead, the preferred v1 architecture is a cluster-based FPGA design that hardwareizes `h_psi`, `s_psi`, `build H_sub/S_sub`, `cdiaghg`, and `refresh/residual -> P_next` inside one hardware-dominant episode path, while retaining a CPU or soft-core companion route only as a fallback contingency. The system under study remains a `QE-connected band-solver subsystem`, not a full DFT SoC and not an isolated reduced-solver chip. The primary comparison object is still the `c_bands episode` under identical QE invocation semantics; the secondary comparison object is the enclosing `SCF iteration` wall time under the same software-visible contract. Validation goal: the SystemC/FPGA study must close the full `rho -> Veff -> while bands not converged { h_psi, s_psi, build H_sub/S_sub, cdiaghg, refresh/residual -> P_next } -> psi -> rho_out` shell with explicit Host / FPGA / off-chip-memory boundaries, and must show that the recommended clustered architecture improves shell-level latency and/or traffic relative to fair `CPU only` and `CPU + GPU` baselines without letting extra diagonalization control, buffering, or synchronization costs erase the gain. A secondary, explicitly testable claim is that `CPU + FPGA` may also offer a stricter and more reproducible `FP64` numerical path than some practical `CPU + GPU` deployments, but this must be validated against declared GPU precision modes and measured through residual, density, eigenspectrum, and iteration-count fidelity metrics. This hypothesis is falsified if hardware `cdiaghg` adds enough traffic, control complexity, or buffering pressure to remove the shell-level win region, or if shell-level convergence behavior deviates materially from the software reference.; sections.experiment.method_or_protocol=Run the evaluation in seven ordered steps. Step 1: freeze the comparison objects, and define the system under study as a `QE-connected band-solver subsystem` rather than a full DFT SoC. Step 2: freeze the workload set using real QE trace cases rather than a single example, and ensure the chosen set spans different `npw`, projector counts, basis sizes, and FFT-grid sizes. Step 3: freeze the comparison metrics, including single `SCF iteration` latency, `c_bands episode` latency, end-to-end wall time, Host-device traffic, FPGA off-chip-memory traffic, stall/utilization, and energy per episode. Step 4: build an analytical per-stage model for the shell, computing `Ops`, `Bytes`, `AI = Ops / Bytes`, `T_compute_lb`, and `T_bw_lb`, so each stage can first be labeled as compute-bound or bandwidth-bound. Step 5: retain the existing body-based SystemC shell model as the software-contract layer, but do not treat its `BODY_01/02/03/04` decomposition as the final hardware implementation. Step 6: freeze a cluster-based hardware architecture with a persistent episode controller, a fused `h_psi + s_psi` operator-sweep cluster, a reduced-matrix build cluster, a hardware `cdiaghg` cluster, and a refresh/residual cluster, together with explicit resident objects, inter-cluster FIFOs, and buffer contracts; keep a companion `cdiaghg` route only as fallback. Step 7: compare the updated `CPU + FPGA` architecture against `CPU only` and `CPU + GPU` baselines using the same QE shell semantics, rather than against theoretical peaks. The current runnable shell model remains `model/qe_band_solver_model`, but the next architecture phase must extend it beyond body-level accounting toward cluster-level design-space exploration.; sections.experiment.evaluation_plan=Freeze the shell-level comparison metrics under the contract defined in `docs/benchmarks/qe_shell_level_comparison_metrics_contract_v0.md`, use `docs/benchmarks/qe_cpu_gpu_fpga_shell_comparison_plan_v0.md` as the Task-6 comparison contract, and use the new clustered-architecture planning note as the implementation-planning contract. Because the proposed system is `CPU + FPGA`, the external baselines that must be beaten or characterized are `CPU only` and `CPU + GPU`; `CPU + FPGA` is the system under study and must be reported using the same shell semantics. Every baseline must report the same case descriptors (`npw`, projector count, subspace sizes, FFT grid, solver path), the same primary performance metrics (episode latency, SCF-iteration latency, wall time, and derived speedups), the same traffic metrics (Host-device traffic, accelerator off-chip-memory traffic, resident/spill accounting where relevant), the same utilization metrics (stall ratio, utilization, overlap efficiency where available), the same analytical quantities (`Ops`, `Bytes`, `AI`, `T_compute_lb`, `T_bw_lb`, bound type), and the same energy-per-episode breakdown when energy is estimated. In addition, the architecture phase must now report hardware-design parameters that were not explicit in the original body model: cluster boundaries, resident objects, buffer capacities, inter-cluster stream widths or queue assumptions, and the hardware-`cdiaghg` versus fallback-companion crossover point. For `CPU + GPU`, results must clearly distinguish `Strict-FP64` and more practical library-oriented GPU modes when both are available; no precision or fidelity advantage may be claimed for `CPU + FPGA` unless the GPU comparison mode is explicitly declared. Fairness is frozen at the shell boundary: count all launch, synchronization, transfer, layout-transform, companion-path, and off-chip-memory costs inside steady-state comparison, while excluding offline build/setup costs from the primary performance numbers. The central question is whether the proposed clustered `QE-connected band-solver subsystem` reduces shell-level wall time and/or system traffic under realistic invocation patterns, not whether it exceeds an abstract GPU peak on isolated kernels. The architecture-planning reference for this phase is `docs/architecture/qe_fpga_clustered_v1_planning_note_20260402.md`.
